record.issuing_body: The White House (President Joseph R. Biden Jr.)
record.summary: The first national security memorandum on AI. It directs the US Government to lead the development of safe, secure and trustworthy AI, to use AI for national security missions only in ways that align with democratic values, and to advance international AI governance. It designates the AI Safety Institute as industry's primary point of contact in government, with mechanisms to partner with national security agencies, makes collection on competitors' operations against the US AI sector a top-tier intelligence priority, and directs a companion Framework requiring risk management, evaluations, accountability and transparency for AI used in national security.
record.notes: Issued 24 Oct 2024 together with the Framework to Advance AI Governance and Risk Management in National Security, which implements it and can be updated regularly. It builds on President Biden's executive order on AI (EO 14110, US-04). NSPM-11 of 5 Jun 2026 (US-28), section 3(f), rescinds and replaces NSM-25 and associated guidance.

verification.note: Recheck of 17 Oct 2026: stored for this record are the White House fact sheet of 24 Oct 2024 on the NARA-archived Biden White House site (stored 11 Oct 2026) and, in this run, NSPM-11 of 5 Jun 2026 from whitehouse.gov. The fact sheet confirms the issue of the NSM on 24 Oct 2024 by President Biden, its three aims, the AI Safety Institute's role and the companion Framework published the same day. NSPM-11, section 3(f), confirms the number 25 and the rescission and replacement of the NSM and associated guidance on 5 Jun 2026. The NSM's own text could not be stored (the archiver could not resolve bidenwhitehouse.archives.gov on 17 Oct 2026), so the full title rests on the record's earlier verification and on the wording of the NSM link on the stored fact sheet. The Framework's URL on ai.gov now redirects to the si.gov home page, so the Framework's text is not stored either; the summary describes the Framework only as far as the fact sheet does.

changes.issuing_body: the fact sheet shows the President issuing the NSM; the stored file does not name the National Security Council as issuer, and the register names the White House and the President for presidential instruments (US-04, US-11)
changes.summary: rewritten from the stored fact sheet: the testing partnerships 'classified and unclassified' and the Framework's prohibited and high-impact use lists are not in the stored file; adds the three aims, the alignment with democratic values and the intelligence priority

judgment.status_reasoning: NSPM-11 of 5 Jun 2026 (whitehouse.gov, stored for this record in this run), section 3(f): 'This memorandum hereby rescinds and replaces National Security Memorandum-25 and associated guidance.' That is the latest event; 'Revoked / withdrawn' stands, with date_last_updated 2026-06-05, the date of NSPM-11.
judgment.scope_reasoning: A presidential memorandum on AI in national security with AI safety and risk-governance content (AI Safety Institute role, risk management Framework); in scope with no note.
judgment.date_reasoning: date_published and date_in_force are 24 Oct 2024, the date of the fact sheet announcing that the President is issuing the NSM 'today'. date_last_updated 2026-06-05 is the date of NSPM-11, the rescinding memorandum, as in other revoked records (US-04 uses the date of the revoking order).
judgment.title_reasoning: The stored fact sheet confirms that this is the National Security Memorandum on AI with the companion Framework to Advance AI Governance and Risk Management in National Security; it does not give the memorandum's full title, which the NSM text requested in extra_urls would confirm. Its link to the NSM text ends in '...memorandum-on-advancing-the-united-states-leadership-in-artificial-intelligence-harnessing-artificial-intelligence-to-fulfill-national-security-objectives-and-fostering-the-safety-security/', which matches the title's wording.

extra_urls.why: NSPM-11, section 3(f), rescinds and replaces National Security Memorandum-25: evidence for status 'Revoked / withdrawn', date_last_updated 2026-06-05 and the number 25 in official_identifier (the same page is US-28's official source).
The NSM's own text, linked from the stored fact sheet ('Read the NSM here'): full title, signature and provisions.
The companion Framework, linked from the stored fact sheet ('Read the frame work here'): its prohibited and high-impact AI uses and risk-management requirements, for the summary and topics.

open_questions: title: the stored files do not give the memorandum's full title (the NSM text on bidenwhitehouse.archives.gov could not be stored; the fact sheet names it only 'National Security Memorandum (NSM) on Artificial Intelligence'). The title stays as published; the link to the NSM on the stored fact sheet follows the title's wording.

The companion Framework's own text is not stored (its ai.gov URL now redirects to si.gov), so its prohibited and high-impact AI use lists, which the earlier summary described, are not in the record any more. A person could provide the Framework PDF with the 'Provide a document' form.
